issues.failure_explanation: In Lemma 4, the generalized eigenvalue problem (4.7) for minimizing backward error has the candidate solution vector parameterized as [-1; y]. The congruence matrix W satisfies W*[0; v_min] = [alpha; v_min]. Equating [alpha; v_min] to a multiple of [-1; y] requires y = -(1/alpha)*v_min, but the proof erroneously asserts that the first component is +1 (and in the subsequent sentence claims that dividing [alpha; v] by alpha yields -1 as the first component), thereby inverting the sign of y and setting x_k = (1/alpha)*Q_k*v_min = -x_k^*. Furthermore, the generalized Rayleigh quotient (4.5) minimizes ||A*x - b||_2 / ||x||_2 rather than the backward error ||A*x - b||_2 / (||A||_2 * ||x||_2), so the minimum singular value sigma_min equals ||A*x_k - b||_2 / ||x_k||_2, meaning berr_{A,b}(x_k) = sigma_min / ||A||_2 rather than sigma_min whenever ||A||_2 != 1. As a result, the returned iterate x_k has the wrong sign (maximizing rather than minimizing residual along that direction) and the reported backward error formula lacks the 1/||A||_2 factor.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: In Lemma 4, Algorithm 1, Theorem 5, and Corollary 1, redefine alpha without the leading minus sign (or set x_k = -(1/alpha)*Q_k*v_min) and divide sigma_min by ||A||_2 (or assume/prescale A so that ||A||_2 = 1, setting the convergence threshold in Algorithm 1 to epsilon * ||A||_2).
issues.overall_effect: Lemma 4 produces an iterate with inverted sign and an unnormalized backward error value. Consequently, Algorithm 1 outputs an incorrect solution with large residual error, its termination check tests an unscaled threshold sigma_min < epsilon, and Theorem 5 and Corollary 1 fail as stated because MINBERR does not achieve the guaranteed backward error.
issues.title: Sign inversion and missing matrix norm normalization in MINBERR reduction
issues.why_classification: A routine sign fix in the solution extraction formula and scaling the threshold/backward error by ||A||_2 completely repairs Lemma 4, Algorithm 1, Theorem 5, and Corollary 1 without changing the proof architecture or weakening the convergence rate or asymptotic complexity guarantees.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The proof of $\berr_{\A,\b}(\widehat\x) = \|\tilde \B_k\widehat{\bf v}\|_2/\|\widehat {\bf v}\|_2$ is as in Lemma~\ref{l:quotient}, noting that $(\widehat\x)_1=-1$.

issues.failure_explanation: In Proposition 1 and its proof in Appendix B, the reduction of the normal-equations generalized eigenvalue problem (B.1) reproduces the same defects as Lemma 4: the vector W*[0; v_min] has first component alpha = -(1/||b||_2)*(B_k)_{1,1}*(v_min)_1, which matches [-1; y] only when y = -(1/alpha)*v_min, yet Proposition 1 claims x_k = (1/alpha)*Q_k*v_min, inverting the sign of the solution. Additionally, the eigenvalue sigma_min is the minimum of ||A*x - b||_2 / ||x||_2, so berr_{A,b}(x_k) = sigma_min / ||A||_2 rather than sigma_min. Hence x_k does not minimize backward error, and Algorithm 2 outputs the negated solution under an unscaled stopping tolerance.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: In Proposition 1 and Algorithm 2, redefine alpha = (1/||b||_2)*(B_k)_{1,1}*(v_min)_1 (or set x_k = -(1/alpha)*Q_k*v_min) and set berr_{A,b}(x_k) = sigma_min / ||A||_2 (testing sigma_min < epsilon * ||A||_2 in Step 5 of Algorithm 2).
issues.overall_effect: Proposition 1 outputs an iterate with inverted sign and incorrect backward error value. Consequently, Algorithm 2 does not minimize backward error over Span(Q_k) and tests an unscaled threshold sigma_min < epsilon rather than sigma_min / ||A||_2 < epsilon.
issues.title: Sign inversion and missing matrix norm normalization in MINBERR-NE reduction
issues.why_classification: A straightforward local sign correction and scaling by ||A||_2 completely restores Proposition 1 and Algorithm 2 without requiring any replacement arguments or loss of advertised claims.
